results.content:
Revix AI is a cloud-based AI code review service for software engineering teams. It connects to GitHub, GitLab.com, or Bitbucket Cloud repositories and analyzes existing code to derive editable review rules based on a team's conventions. For each pull request or merge request, it checks changes against those rules, posts inline comments that explain the issue and reference the applicable rule, and adds a concise change summary to the request. Teams can review and adjust extracted rules, select repositories, and use Revix alongside their existing source-control workflow without adding a CI job. results.content:
## AI code review results after 200 PRs

Revix AI caught 78 issues before merge. Of 216 review comments posted, 151 flagged real issues the team acted on. That is a 70% signal rate.

issues caught before merge
:   78

comments that flagged real issues
:   151/216

signal rate across all review comments
:   70%

These were real issues, not nitpicks. A query that would have missed an index. A retry loop without backoff. An endpoint that skipped the permission check every other endpoint in the module ran.

Signal rate is the metric we watch most, because noise is how AI code review fails.

## Precision beats coverage [...] ## Precision beats coverage

A noisy bot gets ignored. It comments on everything: style opinions, restated diffs, suggestions that contradict how the repo works. After a week, developers scroll past. After a month, someone asks to turn it off.

A reviewer that speaks up 216 times and is right 151 times builds a better habit: people read the comments.

So we tuned Revix AI to stay quiet unless it has something worth saying.

The shape of a comment matters as much as the volume. Each comment opens with a Conventional Comments label such as `issue:` or `suggestion:`, then names the specific behavior and a way out. Our guide to writing a great PR review comment covers the format.

# What 200 Pull Requests Taught Us About AI Code Review

After 200 PRs reviewed by Revix AI, 70% of comments flagged real issues and 129 merge analyses produced 87 new rules. Here's what the data says about where AI code review is headed.

Uri Gonfaus

Uri Gonfaus··Updated

A pull request activity chart showing opened and closed PRs over 30 days

Our AI code review data after 200 pull requests says two things. Precision matters more than coverage. And the most useful learning happens after the code is merged.

Revix AI has now reviewed 200 pull requests. We tracked every comment and every merge from day one.
